key_insight: LUCQUE introduces a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec to support more reliable evaluation of AI tools. It targets gaps in reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment.
problem_solved: Lung cancer screening AI has often been evaluated using private or fragmented public datasets, with inconsistent access to clinical information and expert lung nodule annotations.
method: Build a dataset from low-dose CT (LDCT) scans collected through lung cancer screening in Québec.
Provide comprehensive annotations to address gaps in clinical data and expert nodule labeling.
Support evaluation of screening AI using a consistent dataset; detailed protocols and results are not available in the supplied abstract excerpt.
impact: LUCQUE could help AI/ML practitioners compare screening tools more consistently and conduct reproducible, independent evaluations. The supplied excerpt does not establish dataset access conditions or report benchmark results.
visual_elements: Québec map linked to a lung CT image to illustrate the dataset's origin.
Pipeline diagram: screening LDCT scans → annotated dataset → AI evaluation.
Comparison graphic contrasting fragmented datasets with a unified, comprehensively annotated resource.
Three icons representing reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment.
paper_title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
paper_authors: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemaréchal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas
